title: EIP-8450: Post-Quantum Consensus Key Registry
description: Register dormant hash-based consensus keys for validators and builders ahead of the post-quantum signature switch
author: Thomas Coratger (@tcoratger), Kevaundray Wedderburn (@kevaundray), Tom Wambsgans (@TomWambsgans), Justin Drake (@JustinDrake)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP adds a post-quantum public key registry to the beacon state. Each validator registers two hash-based commitments: a leanXMSS key, which will sign all its messages once duties switch to it, and the 32-byte root of a verifiable random function (VRF) tree, which fixes one verifiable random output per index. Each builder registers only a leanXMSS key. Registration is a new beacon block operation carrying the keys and a proof of possession that binds the leanXMSS key to the registrant's BLS public key. The registrant's BLS signing key authorizes it and can replace registered keys, at a limited rate. The keys stay dormant until a later fork switches duties to them. ## Motivation Every consensus-layer signature today is a BLS12-381 signature: attestations, block proposals, RANDAO reveals, aggregation selection proofs, sync committee messages, payload attestations, inclusion lists, proposer preferences, voluntary exits, the deposit proof of possession, and the execution payload bids and envelopes of builders. BLS relies on the hardness of discrete logarithms in pairing-friendly groups, which Shor's algorithm breaks. A cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) recovers a secret key from its public key, and every validator's and builder's public key is in the beacon state. BLS therefore has to be replaced, and this EIP splits the replacement into two forks. Generating a post-quantum key involves the validator's secret key material, requires new tooling, and, for staking pools, requires coordination between node operators and stake owners. If this work happens at the fork that switches the signature scheme, the number of ready validators is only known at that fork. A separate registry fork has the following benefits: - **Preparation.** Validators generate and register keys, with tooling tested on mainnet, while BLS remains the only scheme used for duties. - **A readiness signal.** The effective balance of active validators with registered keys can be computed from the state, so the switch can be scheduled against an observed threshold. - **Early implementation.** Clients run the hash function, the verifier, and the containers on mainnet before any duty depends on them, since every registration carries a proof of possession. - **A recovery anchor.** If a CRQC appears to be near before the switch, a fork can stop key changes. Keys registered before that fork, while BLS was believed secure, are then the keys the chain moves to, without relying on any BLS signature made afterwards. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). The changes apply to the consensus specifications (`ethereum/consensus-specs`) on top of Heze, and are rebased onto the fork that includes this EIP once it is scheduled. The fork that activates this EIP is assigned by the relevant meta EIP. Functions and constants not defined here keep their meaning from those specifications. The *registrant* of a registration is the validator or builder whose index it names. ### Cryptographic helpers This EIP uses two hash-based primitives, a stateful signature scheme and a verifiable random function (VRF), through the interface below. It specifies the interface and the properties it relies on, not the constructions, so that the registry does not depend on how the primitives are built (see [Interface instead of construction](#interface-instead-of-construction)). Key generation, signing, and opening are not consensus-critical. The signature scheme is leanXMSS and the VRF is a hash-based VRF tree. leanXMSS, with 32-byte public keys and 2404-byte signatures, is implemented in the Cryptography/Xmss module of the ethereum/EthLib repository at commit 6390c73ef040311e807b9047d99dca6b1be1c42f. | Function | Description | | - | - | | `xmss.Verify(public_key: XMSSPublicKey, message: Bytes32, signature: XMSSSignature) -> bool` | Return whether `signature` is a valid signature of `message` under `public_key`, at the leaf index it carries. Return `False`, without raising, for a key or signature that does not decode | | `vrf.Verify(root: VRFRoot, index: Uint32, opening: bytes) -> Optional[Bytes32]` | Return the output of the VRF tree with root `root` at `index` if `opening` is a valid opening of it, and `None` otherwise. This EIP does not call it | A signature carries its leaf index in its first 4 bytes, little-endian. The proof-of-possession check reads it with: ```python def xmss_signature_index(signature: XMSSSignature) -> Uint32: """ Return the leaf index that a signature carries. """ return Uint32(int.from_bytes(signature[0:4], "little")) ``` This EIP relies on the following properties: - **Stateful signatures.** Signatures are unforgeable as long as each leaf index of a key signs at most once. Signing is not assumed to be deterministic, so signing the same message twice at one leaf index is also a reuse. Every leaf index in `[0, 2**32)` can be used. - **Unique VRF outputs.** For a given root and index, at most one output verifies, unless a hash collision is known. An output is unpredictable to others until it is opened. ### Constants #### Domains | Name | Value | Description | | - | - | - | | `DOMAIN_PQ_KEY_REGISTRATION` | `DomainType('0x12000000')` | BLS authorization of a registration by the registrant's signing key | | `DOMAIN_PQ_KEY_POSSESSION` | `DomainType('0x13000000')` | Proof of possession under the registered leanXMSS key | Both domains are computed against the genesis fork version, as for `BLSToExecutionChange`, so that registrations remain valid across forks. #### Registry | Name | Value | Description | | - | - | - | | `PQ_POSSESSION_XMSS_INDEX` | `Uint32(0)` | Leaf index at which the proof of possession is signed | ### Preset | Name | V
